title: America's bases abroad
hook: About 170,000 US troops serve abroad. Half of them are in just two countries.
notes: Troop numbers: active-duty US military personnel by host country on 31 December 2025, from the Defense Manpower Data Center as reported by Reuters, Fox News and USAFacts; they exclude troops on rotation, temporary duty or contingency deployments, so actual presence can be higher. Base locations are a selection of large, publicly known installations, not a complete list.

scenes.title: Where they are
scenes.text: At the end of 2025 about 170,000 active-duty US troops were stationed in other countries. Japan hosted the most, about 54,000, then Germany with 36,000, South Korea 23,000, Italy 13,000 and Britain 10,000.

scenes.title: Europe
scenes.text: Most US forces in Europe date from the Cold War. Ramstein in Germany is the main air hub, Naples hosts the navy's European headquarters, and Rota in Spain and Incirlik in Turkey guard the approaches to the Mediterranean and the Middle East.

scenes.title: Asia and the Pacific
scenes.text: In Japan, US troops are concentrated on the small island of Okinawa. South Korea's Camp Humphreys is the largest US base outside the United States by area. Guam, a US territory, anchors forces further out in the Pacific.

scenes.title: The Gulf and beyond
scenes.text: Around the Persian Gulf, the US runs its regional air headquarters at Al Udeid in Qatar and its Fifth Fleet from Bahrain. Camp Lemonnier in Djibouti is its only permanent base in Africa, and Diego Garcia sits in the middle of the Indian Ocean.
